paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The diagram shows the cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, with the x-axis representing the size of S, denoted as |S|, and ranging from 2 to 10, with a linear scale and no units. The y-axis represents the cosine similarity, with a linear scale, ranging from 0.1 to 0.3, and no units. The diagram features two lines: a blue dashed line representing "Weight averaging" and a green solid line with circle markers representing "QLoRA". The blue line starts at approximately 0.32 at |S|=2 and decreases to approximately 0.26 at |S|=10. The green line starts at approximately 0.28 at |S|=2 and decreases to approximately 0.19 at |S|=10.

model_annotations.English: This plot illustrates the relationship between subset size and average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets and single-task models. The x-axis, labeled $|S|$, has a linear scale with values ranging from 2 to 10, and tick labels are marked at regular intervals of 2. The y-axis, labeled "Cosine similarity", also has a linear scale with values spanning from 0.1 to 0.3, and tick labels are marked at intervals of 0.1. The plot features two lines: one for "Weight averaging" represented by a blue dashed line with square markers, and another for "QLoRA" represented by a green dashed line with circle markers. The blue line begins at approximately 0.32 at $|S|=2$ and decreases to around 0.24 at $|S|=4$, then remains relatively steady around 0.24 as $|S|$ increases to 10. The green line starts at about 0.29 at $|S|=2$, decreases to approximately 0.2 at $|S|=4$, and continues to decrease gradually to around 0.18 as $|S|$ increases to 10.
